basis: Intellectual disability and nail/skin abnormalities define syndrome; VSD and vesicoureteral reflux each 30-79%; foot deformities omitted at cap.
Malignancy arising in the sublingual salivary gland.
Inherited peripheral neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy and foot deformities are characteristic, with amyotrophy reported in 1/1 annotated patients.
Chronic follicular occlusion and suppurative scalp inflammation cause scarring alopecia; secondary infections do not establish a primary infectious mechanism.
Psychiatric umbrella; direct organ damage is not shared across most constituent disorders.
Inborn O-glycosylation disorder; muscular dystrophy/myopathy predominates among constituent subgroups. Brain and eye damage varies by subtype.
Primary liver malignancy; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish disease of skeletal muscle.
Defined by epileptic brain activity and associated neurological dysfunction; systemic causes are subtype-specific.
Astrocytic neoplasm arising in the brainstem.
Testicular germ cell neoplasm affects a reproductive organ; endocrine dysfunction is not intrinsic to this concept.
Defined by abnormal ion-channel function in muscle; neurological, cardiac and immune manifestations depend on subtype.
Glycosylation defect; severe neurodevelopmental disease in 1/1, liver dysfunction and coagulation abnormalities each 30-79%; four-axis cap reached.
Congenital motor-pathway disorder causing mirror movements; bimanual synkinesia reported in 10/18.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in 8/8; nystagmus in 3/8 does not establish direct eye damage.
Leukemia is a malignancy of blood-forming cells; no common direct extrahematologic damage is established for this umbrella.
Skeletal dysplasia; thick skin and progressive valvular disease are core diagnostic features. Respiratory insufficiency and hepatomegaly each 5/19, below threshold.
Defined by sebaceous and speckled lentiginous nevi; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Neurological and ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Cryptococcal fungal infection; pulmonary nodular lesions occur in 30-79%. Annotated meningitis is 5-29% and is also a separately specified subtype.
Premature fusion of cranial sutures is a structural skull disorder; neurological injury is not inherent to every case.
Pancreatic insufficiency and deafness define syndrome; alopecia 80-99%, intellectual disability 30-79%. Lacrimal/endocrine/hepatic findings omitted at cap; liver data from one case.
Congenital fusion of carpal, tarsal and phalangeal bones; hearing abnormality occurs in only 1/20.
Inherited ventricular arrhythmia; associated intrinsic skeletal muscle dysfunction causes proximal weakness in 1/3 annotated patients, just above threshold.
Benign neoplasm confined to the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Defined by congenital structural heart and great-vessel defects; anxiety and depression have no organ axis.
Intellectual disability and congenital eye defects define syndrome; hypogonadism and muscle atrophy/hypoplasia each 30-79%. Cardiac abnormalities 5-29%, excluded.
